title: Beatrix and the Bakery
premise: Jonah Ravensworth, a marine biologist who fled to the coastal town of Marrow Bay after a devastating betrayal, inherits half of an orchard and bakery property alongside Beatrix Calloway, the estranged daughter of the man who ruined her career. The two women are bound by a deed neither can legally break without destroying the other, forcing them into an uneasy partnership restoring the failing orchard before its first harvest. As they uncover evidence that Jonah's old mentor falsified the research that destroyed her reputation—and that Beatrix's father was his accomplice—they must choose between legal vengeance and something harder: forgiveness. In the end, they win back Jonah's name not through the courts but by exposing the truth at the harvest festival, and Jonah finally lets someone stay after the last train leaves.
about_author: Ada Iversen is a former pastry chef turned novelist who writes love stories set in kitchens, coastlines, and the stubborn spaces between people. She lives in a converted orchard house with her partner, two dogs, and a sourdough starter older than their relationship.

chapters.title: Counting Turtles
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. A marine biologist who treats her heart like a specimen to be contained counts sea turtles on Marrow Bay's shore, cataloging her exile in data points. When a lawyer's letter arrives naming her in an inheritance she never expected, her carefully ordered life cracks. Emotional beat: guarded loneliness interrupted by unwanted hope.

chapters.title: The Deed with Two Names
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. Beatrix returns to her late father's orchard expecting sole inheritance, only to find a stranger's name beside hers on the deed—a name she recognizes from the scandal that ended her father's partnership years ago. She arrives at the property to confront the co-heir. Emotional beat: resentment sharpened by grief.

chapters.title: Flour and Salt Water
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. The two women meet on the porch of the crumbling orchard house and discover the deed binds them: neither can sell without the other's consent. Beatrix offers to buy Jonah out; Jonah refuses on principle. They agree to one harvest season together. Emotional beat: hostile truce.

chapters.title: Inventory of Ruins
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Surveying the neglected orchard, Jonah finds her mentor Dr. Edwin Hale's old correspondence hidden in the root cellar—letters suggesting the research fraud that ended her career was orchestrated. She hides the letters from Beatrix. Emotional beat: the past resurfacing like flotsam.

chapters.title: The Bakery That Won't Close
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. Beatrix reopens the attached bakery, her father's true legacy, and finds the town still loves it—and still blames her family for what happened to Jonah. First customers include the widow Marta, who becomes an unexpected ally. Emotional beat: tentative belonging through bread.

chapters.title: Terms of Engagement
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. The women draft a contract dividing labor: Beatrix runs the bakery, Jonah manages the orchard. Their first real collaboration—saving a blighted apple block—reveals each other's competence and stubbornness. Emotional beat: grudging respect taking root.

chapters.title: The Last Train
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Jonah takes the evening train to the county records office and runs into Beatrix, stranded when the last departure is cancelled. Stuck overnight in a station inn, they talk past midnight—first honest conversation about the scandal. Emotional beat: walls lowering in fluorescent light.

chapters.title: What Her Father Buried
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. Digging through her father's study for harvest records, Beatrix finds proof he helped Hale falsify the data that destroyed Jonah's career. Terrified of losing the fragile truce, she conceals it—but starts quietly investigating on her own. Emotional beat: loyalty to the dead versus loyalty to the living.

chapters.title: Blight
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. A fungal blight threatens the entire orchard weeks before harvest; insurance will cover nothing if the crop fails. Working side by side through desperate nights, Jonah and Beatrix move from partners to friends. Marta and the town rally. Emotional beat: found family forming under pressure.

chapters.title: Hale Comes to Town
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Dr. Edwin Hale arrives in Marrow Bay, ostensibly to speak at the university, really to buy the orchard cheaply through a shell company. He offers Jonah her old job back if she sells. She almost says yes. Emotional beat: temptation dressed as rescue.

chapters.title: The Refusal
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. Beatrix discovers Jonah nearly took Hale's deal and confronts her—not with anger but with the truth about her father's guilt, showing Jonah the letters she found. Betrayed that Beatrix hid them for weeks, Jonah walks out. Emotional beat: honesty detonating trust.

chapters.title: Low Tide
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Alone on the shore, Jonah counts turtles and realizes she has been hiding her whole adult life—that invisibility was never safety, just slow drowning. She decides to fight Hale publicly, not for revenge but to reclaim her name. Emotional beat: turning from retreat to resolve.

chapters.title: Amends in Proofing Dough
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. Beatrix leaves an apology in the only language she trusts: a loaf on Jonah's doorstep every morning, each wrapped with a page of her father's confession transcribed by hand. On the fifth day, Jonah knocks on the bakery door. Emotional beat: forgiveness as daily practice.

chapters.title: The Alliance
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Jonah and Beatrix formally ally: they'll expose Hale together using the letters, the confession, and testimony from a retired lab technician Marta knows. They plan to present everything at the harvest festival, where Hale plans to announce his purchase bid. Emotional beat: purpose shared is burden halved.

chapters.title: Gathering Witnesses
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Jonah tracks down Dr. Priya Nair, the technician who was fired after questioning Hale's data. Priya is frightened and bitter, but Jonah's vulnerability—admitting how long she stayed silent too—wins her over. Emotional beat: courage as contagion.

chapters.title: Sabotage
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. Someone torches the bakery's storeroom days before the festival; the fire marshal suspects arson. Beatrix realizes Hale is escalating, and that going public may cost them everything. Jonah refuses to back down. Emotional beat: fear met with defiance.

chapters.title: The Night Before Harvest
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. On the eve of harvest, the town turns out to help pick the orchard by lantern light—Marta, Priya, neighbors, even skeptical farmers. Amid the work, Jonah and Beatrix share a first kiss beneath the oldest apple tree. Emotional beat: abundance as intimacy.

chapters.title: Harvest Festival
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. At the festival, Hale announces his bid. Jonah takes the stage and tells her story; Beatrix reads her father's confession aloud; Priya presents the lab records. The crowd turns. Hale's shell-company buyer withdraws, and the university opens an investigation. Emotional beat: justice outside the law.

chapters.title: Aftermath
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. The fallout ripples: journalists call, the university suspends Hale, and Beatrix grieves her father's memory honestly for the first time. Jonah stays beside her through the worst night without being asked. Emotional beat: grief shared becomes bearable.

chapters.title: The Offer She Doesn't Take
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. The university offers Jonah reinstatement and a prestigious post far from Marrow Bay. Standing in the orchard at dawn, she weighs the life she planned against the one growing here—the bakery's morning smell, Beatrix's laugh, roots. Emotional beat: choosing presence over escape.

chapters.title: Staying Past the Last Train
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Jonah declines the post. On the platform where they were once stranded, she waits for the last train and lets it leave without her, walking back to the orchard house where Beatrix left the porch light on. Emotional beat: love as a decision renewed daily.

chapters.title: First Harvest
chapters.summary: Ensemble close, alternating POV. One year later: the orchard's first full harvest comes in, the bakery expands, Priya visits, Marta presides over the pressing. Jonah and Beatrix sign a new document—not a deed of obligation but a promise, witnessed by their found family. Emotional beat: home as something built together.
